newsitem.title: USA: Campbell shrs seen likely sold by Dorrance.
newsitem.headline: Campbell shrs seen likely sold by Dorrance.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co said it was not involved in a nine-million-share trade of its common stock at $80 per share recorded on the New York Stock Exchange at 1232 EST/1732 GMT Thursday.
Sources agreed the likely seller was John Dorrance III, grandson of Campbell founder Dr. John Dorrance.
In recent months John Dorrance III has been selling huge blocks of equity in the food giant, as detailed in U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings.
Sources said J.P. Morgan handled today's transaction and probably lined up the buyer or buyers.
Campbell shares were trading at 80-3/4, off 2-1/4.

A spokesman at Campbell said Dorrance stated in an SEC 13-D filing in September that he had sold 3.5 million shares in the preceding 60 days, cutting his Campbell stake to 23.4 million shares, or 9.5 percent of the company.
Then in early October, Dorrance filed another 13-D stating he had sold 4.1 million shares since the September filing, dropping his holding to 19.3 million shares, or 7.8 percent, the spokesman said.
"In both those (filings) he said he could sell substantially more shares," the spokesman said.

Today's block trade, equal to 3.8 percent of Campbell's 247 million shares outstanding, was not part of a 13.5 million share buyback at $80 per share announced by the company on October 18, the Campbell spokesman said.
The NYSE said the transaction was the seventh largest block trade in dollar terms ever on the exchange, and the largest in three and a half years.

Dorrance could not be reached for comment. Sources said he is an Irish citizen. The Campbell spokesman said the company does not have any contact with him since he resigned from the board of directors last year.
The lawyer of record on Dorrance's SEC filings also was not available for comment.
The Campbell spokesman said two of Dorrance's siblings and two cousins remain on Campbell's 15-member board of directors.
